The third primitive, `pick_kind_sensitivity`, bridges the two layers by quantifying how spread picks versus total picks respond differently to market information, capturing pick-type specific learning dynamics. Together they map to GSI's conformal prediction and GSE's reinforcement learning frameworks through precise mathematical correspondences.

Later, Dawid's calibration theory (1982) formalized the concept of well-calibrated probability forecasts. More recently, Gneiting et al.'s work on proper scoring rules (2007) provided the foundation for evaluating probabilistic predictions. The current primitives distill these ideas into operationalizable metrics for sports betting.
